title: Parker in New York; buying Tadd Dameron's first arrangement
summary: Parker, Monk and Dameron visit Budd's home, and the Hines sax section's mistake fines pay for Dameron's 'Sweet Georgia Brown'.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Did you see him in New York here?
Oh, yes I saw him in New York. In fact, he used to come around to my house, him and Monk and Tad Dameron and Miles and all of the cats and that. In fact, --

We bought the first arrangement Tad Dameron ever wrote, when he wrote -- when I was with Earl Hines. He's from Cleveland, Ohio, and he was in high school. He was just getting ready to finish high school and he made the arrangement on 'Sweet Georgia Brown.' Well, the reason we

could buy this arrangement was because we had a little thing going in the band, the sax section. Everybody that made a mistake got to pay five cents, or everybody in the brass -- trombone section made a mistake had to pay five cents. Everybody in the trumpet section had to pay five cents. So this money, we would accumulate this money so we could buy our whiskey.
Well, I can also use this money to buy arrangements from any arranger that I, you know, ran across that I wanted to use the money for and buy manuscript paper and whatnot.
Did you know [Hiller?] on 52nd Street, Budd?
I knew them before, way before 52nd Street.
Yeah, but I mean you explain that.

Oh, yes. This was way before 52nd Street. In fact, this was like when we were first forming Earl Hines' band, when we hit Cleveland is when I bought this arrangement off of Tad, 'Sweet Georgia Brown.' And I didn't get to 52nd Street until 1942. This was like back in 1938.
